name: Native
summary: Native application chrome: system typeface, neutral near-white ground with true-white surfaces, hairline separators, one green accent, sentence case throughout, one radius ramp, depth by shadow. Replaces the retired 'Paper Line' world (warm oat ground, terracotta complement, Archivo webfont, letterspaced caps, radius 0, hatch texture).

surface.note: 1.09:1 vs ground — separated by shadow, not tone

accent.note: legal in BOTH directions; this is why there is no deepened text sibling

danger.role: faults only: won't-fit, collision, failed lookup, delete

sep.note: ink at alpha, never a grey paint

typography.fontStack:
-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI Variable Text",
          "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
typography.monoStack: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
typography.letterSpacing: negative only, -.005em to -.028em; nothing positively tracked

radius.note: one ramp, applied everywhere including the schedule

elevation.rule: depth is shadow, never a border

motion.reducedMotion: spatial travel and looping animation stop; opacity/colour state remains

layout.note: Unscheduled lives in the rail, not under the schedule. Sharing the column halved the schedule (425px -> 756px after the move) and created two nested scroll regions.

rules: One Accent Rule — a single green legal as fill-behind-white and as text-on-white; never add a second.
Elevation-Not-Tone Rule — white cards are 1.09:1 on the ground; removing a shadow makes them vanish.
Sentence Case Rule — zero text-transform:uppercase; no positive letterspacing.
System Face Rule — no webfont is loaded.
One Radius Ramp Rule — no raw pixel radii, schedule included.
Danger Reserve — --danger only for real faults.
No Texture — zero background image fills.
Card Stripe Ban — event cards carry no coloured left edge; the track and badge already say it.
Pixel-based drag tests must measure px-per-minute off the live grid; expandRows changes slot height.

exceptions.why: a marker floats over unknown tile content; no tonal step can separate it
